newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator offers oil/natgas tax breaks bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator offers oil/natgas tax breaks bill.

text.p: U.S. oil and natural gas producers would get more lenient tax treatment under a bill offered this week in the Senate.
Oklahoma Republican Don Nickles introduced the bill to allow producers to deduct geological and geophysical costs as an ordinary business expense instead of being treated as a capital expenditure.
The bill also would eliminate the net income limitation on the resource depletion allowance, which Nickles said would encourage producers to keep more marginal wells in operation.
The current net income limitation requires percentage depletion to be calculated on a property-by-property basis and bars percentage depletion that exceeds net income from a particular property.
This "creates a nightmarish quagmire of recordkeeping, paperwork and compliance for taxpayers and the IRS," Nickles' statement said.
The bill also would clarify that delay rental payments made by producers to oil and gas lessors before drilling or production can be deducted.

It also would extend the 90-day prepayment period before drilling starts to 180 days to determine the year in which deductions may be taken, and would include hyrdo injection as a tertiary recovery method under the Enhanced Oil Recovery tax credit.
Similar legislation was introduced last week in the House.
